text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Majority in parliament want elections to individual companies' works councils to take place on the same day across the country. (p1)
- HAL Investments and Willem Sijthoff sign provisional agreement to take over share certificates in the financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad. (p1)
- President-director Willem Smit of Schiphol Airport thinks the cabinet will soon take a decision on privatising the airport. (p1)
- Textile firm Van Heek-Ten Cate takes over loss-making Braat Beheer of Nuenen. (p1)
- Food and drinks concern BolsWessanen talks about selling chocolate unit Luijks Beheer to its management. (p3)
- Publisher Bosch & Keuning is to sell its printing activties to Utrecht-based Brouwer Groep. (p3)
- Germany's chemicals concern Hoechst's Dutch unit Hoechst Holland 1996 net results boosted by windfalls. (p4)
- Dutch consumer spending rose 4.4 pct in volume in January compared with 3.1 pct in the year-earlier period, according to statistics office CBS. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Health minister Els Borst wants to continue her system of contributions for the national health insurance. (p1)
- Talks between unions and Philips Electroncis on Hoogeveen plant fail; strikes start today. (p2)
- Temp agency Randstad's director Frits Goldschmeding wants to stay on as director, even after he will be 65. (p2)
- Swine fever possibly emerges in the province of South Holland. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- According to Dutch legal professor d'Oliveira appears from old laws that Queen Beatrix is an English citizen. (p1)
- Criminals may escape prosecution as Amsterdam court suffers from shortage of staff. (p1)
- Entertainment company Endemol seeks to strengthen its position on the international market through deal with U.S. TV film distributor WIN. (p13)
TROUW
- Dutch army starts action against use of drugs; 10-15 men fired for use. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell enters into agreement with environmental lobby groups in the Netherlands to reduce exhaust of dangerous substances. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Health minister decides not to prosecute chemicals firm Vos for selling the glycerine causing the death of dozens of children in Haiti. (p4)
- Container transshipment ECT talks with Bell Lines about cooperation in transport and handling of containers. (p11)
